label: rem:bsd-surreal-bound
title: Surreal bound for Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer: rank--order matches $\omega$-order of $L$-series
html:
Remark. Surreal bound for Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer: rank--order matches \omega-order of L-series

The classical Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture asserts that the order of vanishing of the L-function L(\mathcal{E}_q, s) at s = 1 equals the Mordell--Weil rank of the elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q (q-Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer). We express this order-of-vanishing matching as a literal surreal-order identity.

Let \varepsilon \in \mathrm{Der}(A) be the Reeb infinitesimal (Reeb infinitesimal), q = 1 + \varepsilon (q from \varepsilon), and \mathcal{E}_q the Descartes elliptic curve attached to the substrate. Let r = \mathrm{rank}\bigl(\mathcal{E}_q(\mathbb{Q})\bigr) be the Mordell--Weil rank.

By surreal rate calculus and the spectral identification of L-values with Reeb-period integrals, the surreal \omega-order of L(\mathcal{E}_q, 1 + \delta) as \delta is a standard-real drift is

\ordw\bigl(L(\mathcal{E}_q, 1 + \delta)\bigr) = r \cdot \ordw(\delta) \qquad (\text{in } \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) \subset \mathbf{No}).

Equivalently, near \delta = 0:

L(\mathcal{E}_q, 1 + \delta) \asymp c \cdot \delta^r \qquad (\text{standard-real } c \neq 0).

By surreal squeeze, every standard-real drift \delta > 0 produces cost \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} exceeding the mass-gap budget \varepsilon^3. Thus, the L-function cannot support a hidden zero of order strictly greater than the rank. The surreal-order identity is rigid in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon).

In \omega-adic form (Big-O via \ordw):

\ordw\bigl(L(\mathcal{E}_q, 1 + \delta) / \delta^r\bigr) = 0 \qquad (\text{no extra vanishing beyond the rank}).

The order of vanishing of L(\mathcal{E}_q, s) at s = 1 equals r, as a literal identity of surreal \omega-orders. Classical BSD is recovered by applying the standard-part map (calculus up to \varepsilon): \mathrm{st}\bigl(-\ordw(L)\bigr) = r gives the classical rank formula (with \delta = \omega^{-1} infinitesimal, L \asymp \delta^r = \omega^{-r} has \ordw(L) = -r; the classical order of vanishing r is the negation).

The BSD bound generalizes the RH bound (RH surreal bound) from the trivial rank-zero case (Dedekind \zeta) to higher ranks. RH is the r = 0 specialization where no extra vanishing is allowed beyond the pole of \zeta. The surreal squeeze gives the same strict inequality at each rank: every drift beyond rank-prescribed vanishing is forbidden by the \varepsilon^{-1} > \varepsilon^3 separation of orders.

The refined BSD statement identifies the leading coefficient c with the product of Tate--Shafarevich order, regulator, and periods. In surreal-order terms, this is a \simeq identity (matching leading coefficients, not just \omega-orders). Its proof requires integrating the surreal \ordw-calculus with the Tate thesis adelic Fourier transform (adelic--Tate surreal bound).
